text: Chickens can receive medicine several ways. Eye drop: often used for vaccination, with the vaccine mixed into a colored (usually dark blue) solvent so the farmer can clearly see the drop land in the chick's eye. Injection: used for vaccines or medicines like antibiotics, given in the breast muscle — some medicines can be toxic if injected in the leg since they go more directly toward the kidneys. Scarification: used especially for the Fowl Pox vaccine, applied in the wing web. In the water: vaccines, antibiotics, and vitamins can be given this way; withholding water for a few hours beforehand makes birds thirsty enough to reliably drink the full dose when it's offered. In the feed: used for medicines that don't dissolve well, or when farmers use human medicines; the key limitation is that sick chickens keep drinking but stop eating, so feed-based dosing may under-treat a sick bird.
